title: Voltage and resistor power
hook: Change voltage magnitude and predict resistor power.
misconception: resistor power doubles when voltage magnitude doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply P = V²/R to compare resistor power when voltage magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ohmic resistor with fixed resistance, P = V²/R. When voltage magnitude doubles, resistor power becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model P = V²/R; scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ohmic resistor with fixed resistance, with a nonzero initial result. If voltage magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on resistor power?
recall.why: Apply P = V²/R under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
